mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or civil registry authority of the UBO's country of nationality, followed by a public notary in that country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the Egyptian consulate/embassy in the country of origin; Egypt is not a contracting state to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so an apostille alone is not accepted for Egyptian GAFI filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and/or Certificate of Incumbency for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry, commercial registrar or corporate affairs authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Egyptian diplomatic mission in that jurisdiction, with prior attestation by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution and power of attorney authorizing the Egyptian LLC incorporation, appointment of local managers, registered office, and designated bank signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or company secretary in the jurisdiction of the appointing corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian consulate/embassy in the appointing shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and account-signature confirmation for each shareholder, director, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed tier-1 commercial bank in the shareholder's or director's country of residence; shell-bank references are not accepted
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing country and the Egyptian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Arabic translation of all consular-legalized corporate documents, passports board minutes and powers of attorney

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified sworn translation attached to the consular-legalized source document; no additional apostille is required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every UBO, director, authorized representative, and beneficial signatory against (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the United States OFAC SDN list; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) the UK OFSI consolidated list; (v) the domestic terrorist-financing and money-laundering lists maintained by EMLCU and the Central Bank of Egypt; (vi) Interpol Red Notices and adverse-media financial-integrity databases; and (vii) FATF public statements identifying high-risk jurisdictions with countermeasures. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence requiring documented source of wealth, source of funds, senior-management approval within the bank or GAFI one-stop-shop process, and transaction monitoring continuing for at least 24 months after PEP status ceases. Screening must be repeated at every ownership transfer, whenever a new manager or authorized signatory is added, and in any event on an annual rolling basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Investor Services Portal / One-Stop Shop electronic name reservation system (gafi.gov.eg), supplemented by the Commercial Registry name-index module operated under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name of an Egyptian LLC must be in Arabic. A Latin/English transliteration is permitted only as a secondary trade name, not as the controlling legal name. The Arabic name must not be identical, phonetically confusing, or visually similar to any name already registered with GAFI or the Commercial Registry, must not incorporate a protected trademark without the owner's consent, and must clearly associate with the legal form 'شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة' (LLC / ذ.م.م). The GAFI comparison matrix treats Arabic orthographic variants, diacritics, singular/plural differences, word order, and transliteration ambiguities as potential conflicts.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested name is rejected, GAFI issues a formal written rejection reason through the Investor Services Portal. The applicant may immediately reserve a pre-selected backup name in Arabic and/or transliteration. To appeal, the applicant must file a written administrative objection with the GAFI One-Stop Shop Complaints Committee within 15 business days of rejection, attaching the GAFI name-conflict search report, trademark availability evidence, and a proposed alternative name. If the complaint is denied, the applicant may submit a second-level administrative appeal to the Minister of Investment or the GAFI Board of Directors within 30 days. A final judicial challenge may be brought before the competent Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council within 60 days after final administrative refusal. Name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days if an extension request is filed before the initial reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure mail-forwarding virtual office is not acceptable for GAFI incorporation, Commercial Registry registration, or Egyptian tax registration. A serviced office is acceptable if it provides a physical registered address in Egypt, a valid lease or service agreement, physical signage listing the company, and practical access for service of process and authority inspections. For an online jewelry and watches e-commerce company, no retail storefront is required, but if the business imports goods under its own customs code, a registered storage or bonded-warehouse address will be required for inventory and VAT compliance; a virtual office alone is insufficient for customs supervision.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% baseline risk of an unannounced physical inspection at the registered office within the first 12 months for an online jewelry/watch merchant. The risk increases to approximately 25-30% if the company claims VAT credits on high-value precious-metal imports, ships inventory from a bonded warehouse, or has cash-remittance or third-party payment-rails concentration. GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the Commercial Registry retain authority to conduct unannounced seat-of-management inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (Limited Liability Company chapter), as amended by Law No. 180 of 2018 and Companies Law No. 8 of 2022; Executive Regulations under Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (GAFI One-Stop-Shop incorporation procedure).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investor Services Center / One-Stop-Shop (OSS), with integrated registration at the Commercial Registry and Egyptian Tax Authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Incorporation Contract (Aqd Al-Ta'sis) of the Limited Liability Company, submitted on GAFI Form No. 1 for LLC establishment, culminating in issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Al-Ta'sis).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to Egyptian LLCs following the Law No. 180 of 2018 amendments; partners freely fix the share capital, which must be adequate for the declared online retail activity. Cash contributions subscribed at formation must be deposited in a temporary blocked account at a Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) licensed bank and are releasable only after the Certificate of Incorporation is issued; in-kind contributions require an independent financial appraiser's report filed with GAFI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST ORGANIZATIONAL RESOLUTION OF THE LLC MEMBERS (Adopted unanimously; English convenience translation for governance records). RESOLVED: (1) That the Members ratify the Incorporation Contract (Aqd Al-Ta'sis) of [Company Name] LLC as filed with GAFI and confirm full subscription of its share capital. (2) That the registered office shall be [street address], Egypt, as recorded in the Commercial Registry. (3) That [Name], [ID/Passport No.], be appointed General Manager of the Company, with exclusive authority to sign contracts, open bank accounts, and file returns. (4) That [Name], [ID], be appointed Compliance Officer for tax, AML, and jewelry-sector disclosures. (5) That the General Manager is authorized to complete OSS formalities and execute any ancillary documents necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Trademark Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center (One-Stop-Shop window or GAFI electronic services portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the LLC name reservation request for a proposed Arabic trade name with an English transliteration, and pay the applicable reservation fee. The reserved name must not be identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered on the Commercial Registry or to a protected trademark in the Egyptian Trademark Registry, particularly in the jewelry, watches, and fashion accessories classes. Obtain the GAFI name reservation certificate, which is valid for the statutory reservation window and must be attached to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Valid passport or national ID copy of each founding partner
Brief statement of the LLC object (online retail of fashion jewelry, fine timepieces, and fashion accessories)
Three alternative trade names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or trademark conflict, the founders may substitute another alternative name from the same application without additional fees or appeal to the GAFI Legal Affairs Committee within 15 business days, attaching evidence of bona fide use or coexistence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the LLC Incorporation Contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian notary / GAFI notarization office (Shahr Al-Aqari for premises components)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain Egyptian counsel to draft the Arabic incorporation contract. All founding partners must appear before the competent notary to authenticate their signatures; the contract must state the object clause (limited to online merchandising of fashion jewelry, watches, and accessories), principal office address, share capital and quota values, management rules, and financial year. If contributions include intangible assets such as domain names, e-commerce platforms, or prepaid stock, attach an independent valuator's report and schedule the in-kind contribution to the contract.
required_dossiers: Passports or national IDs of all partners
GAFI name reservation certificate
Lease agreement or usufruct contract for the registered office
Valuation report for in-kind contributions (if any)
Three signed copies of the Arabic Incorporation Contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary queries a capital provision, object clause, or corporate governance provision, counsel amends the draft, obtains fresh partner signatures, and resubmits; amendments made before final filing carry no penalty and do not reopen the GAFI file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop Submission and Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop (OSS) - Investor Services Center, head office or governorate branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated incorporation contract package at the OSS together with GAFI Form No. 1 (LLC establishment application), pay the consolidated statutory government fees (registration, notarization, and publication components, approximately USD 150), and acknowledge the integrated clearance. The OSS electronically coordinates entry in the Commercial Registry and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation; the Tax Card number and establishment record data are issued simultaneously for the same file. Ensure the object clause expressly states 'online wholesale and retail trading in fashion jewelry, watches, and accessories' to avoid subsequent license queries.
required_dossiers: Notarized Arabic Incorporation Contract
GAFI Form No. 1 (LLC) signed by all partners
GAFI name reservation certificate
Copies of partner passports or national IDs
Registered office lease
Proof of subscription and deposit of cash capital in a CBE-licensed bank (blocked temporary account), if capital was deposited
Valuation report for in-kind contributions (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the OSS issues a query letter due to an incomplete object clause or insufficient capital rationale, counsel has 10 working days to submit a corrective memorandum; upon rejection, the founders may refile after curing the defect or appeal to the GAFI Ministerial Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Tax Card, and VAT/Electronic Invoicing Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - tax office competent for the registered address (via GAFI OSS integration where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the ETA registration application to obtain the Tax Card (Al-Bitaka Al-Daribiya), register for VAT where the LLC's annual taxable supplies meet the mandatory threshold applicable to e-commerce retailers, and onboard the ETA electronic invoicing and e-receipt system before issuing B2B or B2C documents. Establish payroll withholding registration for employees and register any excise-relevant goods handling if the product mix includes imported luxury articles subject to customs or consumption duties.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Tax Card application (ETA Form)
Commercial Registry extract
Registered office lease
Partners' IDs, passports, and prior tax numbers (if any)
Bank account details
Electronic signature certificate and e-invoicing onboarding forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Card is withheld due to a pending social insurance issue or a prior tax history query against a partner, supply the ETA with the clearance certificate or settle the contested amount under protest; administrative objection must be filed within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance (NOSI) Establishment Registration and Workforce Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) - local branch; Ministry of Manpower for work permits and occupational health clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon the first hire, register the LLC with NOSI on Form 1 (establishment record) and Form 2 (insured persons) within 30 days of the employment start date, obtain the employer file number for payroll contributions, and enter the e-contribution cycle for monthly declarations. For expatriate personnel, secure work permits and residency stamps from the Ministry of Manpower and the Passport and Immigration Authority before commencement of duties.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Tax Card
Commercial Registry extract
Lease or title document for the premises
Employment contracts
Passports and work permits for foreign staff (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Delays in issuance of the NOSI file number do not suspend operations; the employer may file a declaration under Law No. 79 of 1975 and pay contributions retroactively, curing any lapse by payment of the prescribed NOSI late surcharge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Capital Release, and Payment Service Provider Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CBE-licensed commercial banks (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, CIB); CBE AML/CFT framework for customer due diligence; payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) for merchant onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, the First Organizational Resolution appointing bank signatories, and the KYC files of all managers and beneficial owners to the chosen licensed bank. Because online jewelry retail is a Medium-Risk Enhanced AML category, submit source-of-wealth declarations and complete enhanced customer due diligence; where the formation capital was held in a blocked temporary account, the bank releases the funds to the LLC's operational account upon presentation of the Certificate of Incorporation. Use the same documentation set for onboarding with Stripe, PayPal, or their licensed regional processing partners, and complete the PCI-DSS SAQ-A for card-not-present transactions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Tax Card and ETA registration documents
Commercial Registry extract
First Organizational / Board Resolution appointing signatories
Passports or national IDs and source-of-wealth statements of all ultimate beneficial owners
Business plan and forecast transaction volumes for jewelry and watches
PCI-DSS attestation for the e-commerce payment environment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects the file due to enhanced due diligence concerns, submit the file to two alternative banks; for unjustified refusals, the CBE complaint unit may review upon written application. Where Stripe or PayPal cannot onboard the Egyptian entity directly, engage a licensed MENA/EU payment facilitator that underwrites the merchant and performs acquisition under the card network's rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; online portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg (e-invoicing/clearance: https://einvoice.eta.gov.eg)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must apply for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) at the ETA’s taxpayer registration department before engaging in taxable activities. Submission via the ETA portal or local tax office includes the certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, commercial registration extract (current trade registry certificate), power of attorney, passport copies of managers/shareholders, registered office proof, and estimated activity description. The ETA issues the TIN and, separately, a VAT (Sales Tax) registration certificate once the EGP 500,000 compulsory VAT threshold is met or on voluntary application; a non-resident vendor with an Egyptian sales nexus may be required to register and appoint a tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the LLC is a separate taxable juristic person under Egypt Law No. 91 of 2005; no pass-through to shareholders. Resident LLCs pay corporate income tax on worldwide income; foreign LLCs are taxed on Egypt-source income only. Ordinary LLCs are not within the Suez Canal Economic Zone tax-exemption regime unless specially licensed within that zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election is available under Egyptian domestic law. An Egyptian LLC is per se opaque and must file corporate income tax. ETA allows a tax group/consolidated return election for a parent and its at-least-90-percent-owned Egyptian subsidiaries, subject to ETA approval. For VAT purposes, an LLC may elect voluntary registration below the statutory threshold but cannot elect to be treated as non-taxable once the threshold is exceeded.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – Egypt VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 and its Executive Regulations, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority with e-invoice/e-receipt clearance
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies (goods and services) for compulsory VAT registration; voluntary registration is available for lower-turnover persons, and non-resident suppliers of goods/services to Egyptian customers may be registered and required to appoint a fiscal representative under the Executive Regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Since October 2020, VAT-registered taxpayers are integrated into ETA’s real-time e-invoice/e-receipt system phased by turnover. Invoices must be generated through an ETA-certified billing system or the ETA portal in XML/JSON format, digitally signed with the taxpayer’s certificate, assigned a unique invoice UUID/QR code, and submitted to the ETA for fiscal validation (clearance) before or immediately upon issuance. ETA API integration is mandatory for high-volume taxpayers; no paper or handwritten invoices are accepted for the scope of this compliance profile once the electronic mandate applies to the taxpayer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAT-registered Egyptian LLC may zero-rate the export of goods where sale and title transfer are made to a non-resident buyer and the goods physically leave Egypt under customs control within the legally required export period. Exported services are zero-rated where the recipient is outside Egypt and the service is actually performed/used outside Egypt in accordance with the Executive Regulations. The exporter must retain complete evidence of export and receipt of hard-currency consideration; absent such evidence the supply is taxed at 14%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outward customs statement) bearing the ETA/customs release stamp
Commercial invoice and matching VAT e-invoice code from the ETA e-invoicing system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an Egyptian bank classifying the transaction as export proceeds
Underlying export contract/purchase order, and Letter of Credit or SWIFT payment instruction when applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audit teams verify zero-rated export claims against customs exit data, invoices, and bank foreign-currency records. If documents are incomplete, export is not proven, or export proceeds are not repatriated through Egyptian banks within the 180-day deadline, ETA may issue a revised assessment re-characterizing the supply as taxable at 14%, charge late-payment interest/damages, and levy administrative fines. Fraudulent or false zero-rating documentation is treated as tax evasion: the VAT is clawed back with heavy monetary penalties and possible criminal prosecution, and the taxpayer’s e-invoicing clearance privileges may be suspended.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the sole statutory authority for monetary policy, foreign exchange control, and banking supervision under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), operating the official unified exchange rate regime and the International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) for all cross-border fund movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains open current-account convertibility following the 2016 exchange rate float and the March 2024 unification of the exchange rate, under which the EGP is convertible at the banking-system rate for genuine current-account transactions, including trade services, profit remittances, and dividend repatriation. Capital-account flows such as equity injections, shareholder loans, and repatriation of invested capital remain subject to CBE-supervised bank verification, source-of-funds documentation, and balance of payments purpose coding, with no general ex-ante licensing outside regulated sectors; practical hurdles include periodic commercial-bank foreign-currency liquidity pressure, documentary rigidity (repatriations must be matched to prior inward remittance declarations and, where applicable, the investment registration certificate issued under Law No. 72 of 2017), and the requirement that profit remittances flow only through the Egyptian banking system after verification of audited accounts, tax clearance, and corporate approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt and credited to an account with a CBE-licensed bank within the contractual settlement window not exceeding 90 days from the shipment date; each receipt must be declared under the CBE ITRS with the underlying customs and export documentation. Following the March 2024 exchange-rate unification, the CBE has suspended mandatory percentage surrender requirements (the prior managed-rate regime had imposed temporary conversion ratios of up to 15% on export revenues); exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in foreign-currency Export Proceeds Accounts or convert into EGP at the unified banking rate, provided the full amount is routed through the formal banking system. Failure to repatriate within the timeline triggers bank compliance holds, EGP conversion penalties, and tax-authority scrutiny.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for share-capital remittances; multi-currency Operational Current Account with dedicated export-proceeds and trade-finance desks
Operational Current Account (EGP/USD/EUR) bundled with e-commerce gateway settlement and documentary collection facilities
Operational Current Account with premium FX desk, SWIFT MT103/MT700 execution, and corporate treasury products
Export Proceeds Account and pre-shipment/post-shipment trade-finance facilities for jewelry and timepiece exporters
Multi-currency Operational Account with global correspondent clearing and FX hedging lines
Operational Current Account with retail payment-acquiring and payroll services
Operational Current Account for EGP treasury and corporate card programs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium (restricted). Offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not authorized by the CBE to open standalone clearing or collection accounts for an Egyptian-domiciled LLC or to execute EGP settlement outside the licensed banking system, due to the extraterritorial scope of Law No. 194 of 2020 and the AML/CFT Law No. 80 of 2002. Their lawful use is limited to ancillary merchant-payout aggregation (Stripe/PayPal marketplace settlements) that onward-routes via SWIFT into the LLC's CBE-licensed Egyptian bank account; each aggregated inflow must be declared as export proceeds with full payout-ledger evidence. A fintech EMI may serve as a supplementary receivables-matching rail, but the primary treasury, FX conversion, and outgoing trade-payment rails must remain with an Egyptian commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default norm: the CBE AML framework and Egyptian banking practice require at least one authorized signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to appear in person at the bank's branch for biometric identity verification and a compliance interview before account activation; remote video-KYC is accepted only for already-banked clients updating mandates, not for first-time onboarding of Medium_Risk_Enhanced e-commerce entities. Non-resident directors who cannot attend may be accommodated by a notarized power of attorney (translated into Arabic, legalized/apostilled) naming an Egyptian-resident co-signatory, supplemented by a board resolution on account opening, certified memoranda, and the CBE-mandated beneficial-ownership declaration; the compliance officer may, at its sole discretion, still require a one-time video interview with each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Precious-metals trade typology: fungible high-value goods, hallmarking opacity, and supply-chain documentation gaps commonly trigger enhanced due diligence for gold and jewelry merchants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Egyptian Mineral Resources Authority (EMRA) registration/permit (where applicable); certified hallmark certificates and assay certificates per consignment; supplier invoices matched to customs declarations (CargoX/Nafeza ACI records); fully bank-funded payment trail via SWIFT statements; and a signed internal precious-metals compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce aggregator exposure: Stripe and PayPal co-mingled settlements, high refund/chargeback ratios, and absence of per-transaction customs records raise diversion-of-export-proceeds concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Read-only API access to Stripe/PayPal settlement ledgers; monthly payout-to-bank reconciliation statements; merchant-of-record agreements with the aggregators; refund and dispute-resolution register; board-approved e-commerce treasury policy; and export invoice-to-payout matching schedules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and source-of-wealth opacity: non-resident shareholders holding qualifying control without audited financials, causing banks to reject or file Suspicious Activity Reports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE-compliant beneficial-ownership declaration forms; apostilled/legalized corporate registers from the shareholders' jurisdictions; shareholder source-of-wealth statements supported by home-country bank references; audited financial statements of the shareholder entities; and a notarized declaration of no adverse media or sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-office and operational mismatch: an Egyptian LLC registered at an agent's address while business operates abroad, triggering address-verification and tax-residence queries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial registry extract reflecting the LLC's true registered address; translated lease contract or office-space agreement; utility bills (electricity/telecom) in the LLC's name; CATR tax card (mCard); and a board resolution confirming the operational premises and warehouse locations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Untraceable capital injection: shareholder funds arriving from high-risk jurisdictions or via personal accounts without equity documentation, causing incoming-wire holds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' capital-subscription resolution; LLC amendment/Articles of Association evidencing issued capital; notarized declaration of source of funds; SWIFT MT103 evidence from the remitting bank; CBE foreign-investment declaration forms filed by the receiving bank; and, where applicable, the Certificate of Registration issued under Law No. 72 of 2017.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: shareholders execute a capital-subscription resolution and remit via SWIFT MT103 (values above USD 100,000 should use MT202 cover through a correspondent bank). The purpose code must reflect direct-investment equity capital under the CBE ITRS classification; the receiving Egyptian bank is required to obtain the LLC's commercial registration, tax card, and stamped memorandum evidencing the capital increase, and to file the inbound capital declaration with the CBE before crediting the Capital Escrow Account. Funds may be retained in foreign currency or converted into EGP at the unified banking rate; each injection must be mirrored in the commercial-registry capital records and the annual financial statements, as the bank will require these proofs before any later dividend or capital repatriation. Verification stack: MT103 confirmation, shareholder resolution, source-of-funds declarations, and the bank's inward-remittance certificate; the LLC must not split remittances artificially to bypass CBE reporting thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements to overseas jewelry and timepiece suppliers should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for open-account and cash-against-documents (CAD) settlements, and through SWIFT MT700 for irrevocable commercial letters of credit on high-value consignments; documentary collections (D/P and D/A) may be used via MT400 where suppliers accept draft terms. Every outbound remittance requires the CBE import purpose code, the underlying purchase order and commercial invoice, transport documents (air waybill or bill of lading), the Nafeza national-single-window ACI release/customs declaration reference, and proof of any required Egyptian Customs tariff registration; banks also apply their internal FX-availability queue, giving priority to LC-backed and high-frequency CAD flows. For fine-timepiece imports above USD 50,000, a confirmed irrevocable LC is recommended to mitigate counterparty risk, while open-account MT103 remains efficient for repeat suppliers with established trade history.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (outright forwards) with the LLC's CBE-licensed relationship bank, permitted only for genuine current-account hedging against USD/EGP or EUR/EGP trade exposure, supported by underlying invoices and the CBE ITRS declaration.

Cross-currency swaps between EGP and hard-currency flows executed through a CBE-licensed bank as an asset-liability management tool for matched export-receipt and import-payment tenors, subject to bank ALCO approval and CBE monitoring.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the EGP, permitted only where structured by an Egyptian licensed bank and booked as a true hedge of forecast export proceeds; speculative offshore NDF exposure by a resident LLC is prohibited under CBE regulations.

Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put spreads) available from international-tier Egyptian banks for premium-budgeted hedging of seasonal watch and jewelry inventory purchases, with immediate documentation of the commercial underlying.

Commodity-linked forward or fixed-price supplier contracts for gold bullion and precious-metal inputs, not a regulated FX instrument but a permissible physical-price hedge for jewelry manufacturing treasury.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry (within the Civil Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest and administrative fines; prolonged non-payment leads to suspension and strike-off from the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewed annually prior to the expiration date shown on the tax card; generally due within the first month of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of the tax card, impeded customs clearance, blocked tender participation, and per-day late fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Company Registration Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end (i.e., by June 30 for a calendar-year entity), after approval by the shareholders' general assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines as assessed by GAFI, administrative suspension of the company's registration, and potential judicial strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Unit (notifiable record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary of incorporation or upon any share transfer, whichever is earlier; no separate filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002; administrative strike-off for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian limited liability companies, regardless of revenue or asset size, must appoint a licensed statutory auditor and file audited financial statements annually.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) substantially aligned with IFRS, as issued and enforced by the Egyptian Financial Supervisory Authority and GAFI.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once a year, the LLC must verify and update the Ultimate Beneficial Owner register for any changes arising from share transfers, subscriptions, or other ownership movements; updated declarations must be submitted to GAFI within 30 days of the triggering event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and their Powers

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT rate is 22.5% under Law 91/2005 as amended by Law 30/2020. Investment incentives under Law 72/2017 include exemption of export-oriented free-zone profits, an investment-cost deduction of 30%-50% for incentivized projects in designated governorates, and customs privileges; small and micro enterprises under Law 152/2020 may elect turnover-based taxation at 0.5%-1.0%; listed companies with at least 15% public float are taxed at 19.5%. For the subject LLC engaged in online jewelry and watch merchandising, preferential relief applies only where the project obtains Investment Law registration and demonstrates qualifying export profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 21 (Corporate Income Tax Return) e-filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) online e-filing portal at www.eta.gov.eg; supplementary monthly withholding declarations are filed on Form 41 through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final CIT return plus four quarterly advance quota declarations and payments, each equal to 25% of the prior year's net CIT liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final annual return must be filed within four months after the end of the fiscal year pursuant to Law 91/2005 Article 57; for a calendar-year LLC the deadline is 30 April. Quarterly advance quota installments fall due at the end of March, June, September and December of the current tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the LLC, ETA tax card number, commercial registry number, authorized signatories, fiscal year-end and principal place of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Egyptian LLC's tax card and ETA registration code; disclose all non-resident shareholders holding 10% or more economic rights in the beneficial ownership annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross Sales and Egyptian-Source Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross proceeds from online and physical retail of fashion jewelry, watches, accessories and related shipping/insurance surcharges, including Egyptian-source revenue settled through Stripe, PayPal or other payment rails.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attribute all proceeds to the resident Egyptian LLC; commissions or payment-processing credits diverted to offshore accounts remain taxable Egyptian-source income under the artificial-profits rule of Law 91/2005 Article 4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, import duties, platform commissions, payment-processing fees, logistics, payroll, rent, depreciation and statutory social insurance and stamp tax expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Permit deductions only where supported by valid e-invoices, customs declarations and bank records; intercompany service charges require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation to be deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Net Taxable Income Before Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit reconciled to taxable income before special deductions, excluding exempt income and applying the arm's length standard to related-party transactions in precious metals, gemstones and marketing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure intercompany purchase prices for jewelry and watch merchandise are benchmarked; pricing variances exceeding ETA tolerance levels attract transfer pricing review and adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Adjustments and Loss Carryforward Set-Off
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for non-deductible entertainment exceeding the statutory cap, penalties, tax provisions, excessive intercompany charges and other disallowed items; offset of prior-year taxable losses limited to a five-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a copy of the Local File, or the ETA-approved information disclosure form, where aggregate related-party transactions exceed EGP 5 million annually; document any DTA-based allocation of head-office costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Final Tax, Advance Credits and Net Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT at 22.5% on adjusted taxable income, reduced by quarterly advance quota payments and by final withholding tax credits evidenced by Form 41 and Form 20 certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile withholding certificates issued by Egyptian merchants and payment processors; any excess WHT is refundable or creditable to the next quota installment upon ETA verification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of EGP 500-5,000 and a monthly late-payment surcharge of 1% on the unpaid tax, capped at 100% of the tax due; late payment accrues a 1% monthly surcharge on the shortfall; non-filing allows the ETA to issue an estimated assessment with a 50% uplift under Article 131; willful evasion is sanctioned under Article 133 by imprisonment of 3-5 years and a fine of one to three times the evaded tax.
